title: Formal Verification of AI Agent Tool Calls: Can Lean 4 Specify Safe Tool-Call Sequences?

original_idea.body:
# Formal Verification of AI Agent Tool Calls: Can Lean 4 Specify Safe Tool-Call Sequences?

**Problem:** AI agents executing tool calls (file I/O, network, code execution) can cause irreversible harm. Whether Lean 4 formal specifications can express and verify safety properties of tool-call sequences (e.g., 'never delete a file without prior confirmation') is unexplored.

**Direction:** Model 10 AI agent scenarios as state machines. Write Lean 4 specifications for safety properties (reachability, invariants, forbidden states). Attempt to prove these properties using Lean 4. Measure which agent safety properties are expressible and provable in Lean 4's type theory.

**Why it matters:** If formal methods can verify AI agent safety properties at the specification level, this provides a rigorous complement to runtime guardrails. This connects the formal verification field directly to AI agent safety.

**Relevant context:** Claude Code (Anthropic) executes tools with significant system access. Lean 4's dependent types can express state machine properties. No work applies formal specification to AI agent tool-call safety.
